findings.title: codemie-claude --silent still prompts and rewrites settings
findings.problem: canPrompt is computed as canPromptForProject({ task }) && adapter.name !== 'claude-acp'. canPromptForProject only checks --task, CODEMIE_NO_PROMPTS and TTY, and options.silent is never consulted, so `codemie-claude --silent` at a TTY with Bedrock set in Claude settings shows the prompt and can back up and rewrite files. The spec defines canPrompt as canPromptForProject plus ACP and --silent, and AC3 lists --silent among stops that leave files byte-identical. The gate's own doc comment lists --silent as a cause of canPrompt=false.
findings.impact: A user or wrapper that passed --silent expecting no interaction gets an interactive prompt that can consent to rewriting shared Claude settings, contradicting AC3 and the spec's single can-we-prompt rule.
findings.check_notes: AgentCLI.ts:338-342 canPrompt now also requires !options.silent and !options.printConfig; test covers silent and plain TTY run

fix.change: AgentCLI canPrompt now also requires !options.silent and !options.printConfig
fix.test: AgentCLI-bedrock-gate.test.ts: passes canPrompt=false for --silent at a terminal, and true for a plain interactive run

findings.title: Default managed-settings.d derivation never asserted
findings.problem: managedDropInDirs(platform) and the resolver's derive-from-managedFiles fallback are never asserted by any test: every drop-in test injects tmp dirs explicitly, and the only default-path test asserts Array.isArray on the result. A typo or broken derivation would leave real managed drop-ins unread without any test failing. The current production derivation is correct (win32 paths use forward slashes, so posix.dirname is sound).
findings.impact: A regression in the default drop-in directory would make a managed policy enabling Bedrock via managed-settings.d invisible to the gate, so Claude traffic could bypass the gateway while the user believes the switch worked.
findings.recommendation: Export managedDropInDirs and assert per platform (linux /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.d, darwin /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.d, win32 C:/Program Files/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.d and C:/ProgramData/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.d); add a resolver test passing managedFiles without managedDropInDirs that yields a conflict-managed verdict from a drop-in.
findings.check_notes: managedDropInDirs exported and asserted for linux, darwin, win32; resolver test covers derivation from managedFiles with no drop-in dirs given

fix.change: managedDropInDirs exported; resolver fallback derivation covered
fix.test: claude-settings-env.test.ts: derives the default managed-settings.d directories per platform; resolver.test.ts: derives the drop-in directory beside each managed file

findings.title: Connect guidance omits two residual bypasses
findings.problem: The spec requires connect guidance to state three residual bypasses: a Bedrock project elsewhere is not seen, Desktop managed policy on macOS/Windows is not detected, and --settings is not read. connectSentence() states only the first, and only inside stopGuidance, so a connect run that switches and proceeds states none of them.
findings.impact: Users of proxy connect are told the switch is complete without learning about the cases where Bedrock can still bypass the gateway.
findings.recommendation: State all three residual bypasses in connect guidance and surface them on connect runs that switch and proceed, not only in stopGuidance.
findings.check_notes: connectSentence now states all three residual bypasses and promptLines includes them for connect flows, so switch-and-proceed runs show them; tests added

fix.change: connectSentence states all three residual bypasses and the switch prompt of connect flows includes them
fix.test: prompt.test.ts: states all three residual bypasses for connect flows only; states the residual bypasses in the switch prompt of a connect run

findings.title: Bedrock model-id pattern misses jp./au./us-gov. and gov/cn ARNs
findings.problem: BEDROCK_MODEL_ID only recognises us./eu./apac./global. prefixes and arn:aws:bedrock:. Cross-region profiles such as jp.anthropic., au.anthropic., us-gov.anthropic. and ARNs under arn:aws-us-gov / arn:aws-cn are not matched, so isModelId returns false for them and stripClaudeJson/stripVscode leave those model keys in place after the switch.
findings.impact: After a switch the gateway receives a Bedrock model id it cannot serve and the session fails; AC5 (no Bedrock-ID model key remains in any editable layer) is not met for these regions.
findings.check_notes: BEDROCK_MODEL_ID accepts jp./au./us-gov. style prefixes and any arn:aws*:bedrock partition; provider tests extended

fix.change: BEDROCK_MODEL_ID accepts any 2-3 letter (and -gov) region prefix and aws-us-gov / aws-cn ARNs
fix.test: provider.test.ts: isModelId matches jp./au./us-gov. ids and gov/cn ARNs

findings.title: resolveProviderConflict exceeds 50-line limit
findings.problem: code-quality.md Code Structure Guidelines say functions stay under 50 lines and Best Practices list 100+ line functions as a Don't; resolveProviderConflict (lines 280-392) is about 112 lines and mixes input defaulting, parallel reads, managed-chain assembly, per-flow chain construction, warning collection and verdict computation.
findings.impact: A documented code-quality rule is broken in newly added code, which the standards review treats as blocking for the workflow.
findings.recommendation: Split into helpers, for example readAllSources, buildManagedChain, buildChainsForFlow and computeVerdict, so each stays under 50 lines.
findings.check_notes: resolveProviderConflict split into readAllSources, buildManagedChain, buildClaudeChain, buildChains, collectWarnings, computeVerdict; each well under 50 lines

fix.change: resolveProviderConflict split into readAllSources, buildManagedChain, buildClaudeChain, buildChains, collectWarnings, computeVerdict

findings.title: SwitchBlockedError prints raw layer path unsanitized
findings.problem: SwitchBlockedError interpolates resolution.unknownReason into its message. That reason is built in resolver.ts with the raw layer.path and is printed by the AgentCLI and connect catch paths without sanitizeDisplayText. The resolver's malformed-file logger.warn also logs the raw path. The spec requires printed paths and key names to go through sanitizeDisplayText.
findings.impact: A crafted project path containing terminal control characters could reach the user's terminal in the changed-while-running case; the spec's display-sanitization requirement is only partly met.
findings.recommendation: Pass the detail through sanitizeDisplayText inside SwitchBlockedError (or sanitize unknownReason at the source in resolver.ts) and sanitize the path in the malformed-file warning.
findings.check_notes: SwitchBlockedError, resolver unknown reasons and malformed warning all pass through sanitizeDisplayText; tests assert no control characters

fix.change: resolver unknownReason and malformed warning sanitize paths and key names at the source; SwitchBlockedError sanitizes its detail
fix.test: resolver.test.ts: neutralises control characters in the unknown reason and the malformed warning; switcher.test.ts: neutralises control characters in the detail of a blocked switch

findings.title: applySwitch exceeds 50-line limit
findings.problem: code-quality.md requires functions under 50 lines; applySwitch (lines 369-427) is about 59 lines covering re-resolve, target collection, backup, the per-file write loop and restore reporting.
findings.impact: A documented code-quality rule is broken in newly added code.
findings.recommendation: Extract the write-and-restore loop (for example writeTargets) and the backup step into helpers so applySwitch drops under 50 lines.
findings.check_notes: backupTargets and writeTargets extracted; applySwitch now orchestrates in about 35 lines

fix.change: applySwitch extracted backupTargets and writeTargets helpers

findings.title: install claude does not reprint backup folder on later failure
findings.problem: applyBedrockConsent discards result.backupDir, so when agent.install, installVersion or additionalInstallation fails after the switch, the catch block only calls spinner.fail and rethrows. The spec requires a later failure in the same flow to print the backup folder again; AgentCLI.ts and connect-orchestrator.ts do.
findings.impact: A user whose install fails after their Claude settings were stripped is not told where the backup is, which the spec treats as the recovery path.
findings.recommendation: Keep result.backupDir from applyBedrockConsent and print `Backup of your Claude settings: <dir>` in the install failure paths before rethrowing.
findings.check_notes: install.ts keeps settingsBackupDir and prints it on additionalInstallation and install-path failures, once per path; tests added

fix.change: install keeps result.backupDir and prints 'Backup of your Claude settings: <dir>' on install and additionalInstallation failures
fix.test: install.bedrock-gate.test.ts: prints the backup folder when the install fails after a switch; when additionalInstallation fails; prints none when nothing was switched

final_round.rationale: All four lenses and standards ran; 8 blocking findings (1 critical: codemie-claude --silent still prompts despite the spec's canPrompt rule). 0 deferred; 23 candidates dismissed as noise (e.g. win32 managed drop-in path concern disproved because the paths use forward slashes, Editor sort order protected by push order, desktop key removal is spec-designed).
